subject: geography
title: Drainage Basin: Stores Fill in Sequence, the River Lags

segments.say: The storm arrives and interception fills first. The rain falls on the whole basin, but the interception store catches it and only spills once full, so the channel and the hydrograph stay flat. Point at the interception store on your student notes diagram before any water moves on.
questions: Which store fills first when the storm arrives?
What does the hydrograph do while the first store fills?

segments.say: Soil fills next and groundwater starts last. The full interception store spills, the spill infiltrates into the soil store, and slow percolation only now starts feeding the groundwater store. Now try the sequence questions on your worksheet.
questions: In what order do the three stores fill?

segments.say: Soil saturates, overland flow peaks the river late. At saturation the surface flow switches on, discharge rises fast, and the peak arrives after the rain itself has eased. Check the lag against your student notes before moving on.
questions: What switches on when the soil store saturates?
Why does the discharge peak come after the peak rain?

segments.say: Rain gone, the river recedes slowly on baseflow. The surface stores drain, but groundwater keeps feeding the river, so the fall is slow. Keep the interception, soil, groundwater order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What sustains the river after the rain has gone?
What are the four stages of the storm pulse, in order?
segments.watchFor: The river peaks when the rain is heaviest, because rain runs straight off the surface into the river. Listen for students who put the discharge peak at the heaviest rain, or let rain run straight off the surface before the soil saturates. Send them back to scene 1 and the flat hydrograph while interception fills: The basin stores fill in sequence - interception first, then the soil store, then groundwater - and overland flow only switches on once the soil saturates, so discharge peaks after the peak rain and then recedes slowly, sustained by groundwater baseflow.
